text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- The Yugoslav parliament will convene on July 15 to determine the list of candidates for Yugoslav president. The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia has proposed Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as its candidate but has not yet officially submitted his candidacy to parliament.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic rejected president Milosevic's invitation to come to Belgrade in view of her two-hour detention at Belgrade airport a week ago and called for talks to be held in Banja Luka.
- Some 1,500 Zastava arms factory workers of Kragujevac gathered in front of the city hall on Tuesday demanding payment of overdue wages.
- U.N. Administrator for Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein said in Belgrade demilitarisation of the area is a key to stability.
- The people, the army and the international community are on the side of Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic, says her adviser Ana Mitrovic.
- Former Bosnian Serb army commander general Ratko Mladic was seen on holiday on the Montenegrin coast, local villagers report.
- Croatian oil industry INA general manager announced the company would seek return of its petrol stations in Yugoslavia.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav and Dutch businessmen discussed cooperation in construction of greenhouses in Yugoslavia.
- Nis tobacco industry DIN resumed production after a three week break caused by poor sales due to large quantities of smuggled cigarettes on the market.
BORBA
- Federal hydrometeorological institute warned of the abrupt increase of the Danube river water levels due to heavy rains. Special flood protection measures to be taken downriver from Bezdan.
- Recycling Agency draws up a unified waste management programme in cooperation with the Serbian environment ministry.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- The Serbian cancer and radiology institute has postponed all surgeries except the most urgent ones due to lack of anaesthetics.
- Bosnian Cardinal Vinko Puljic will meet Serbian Patriarch Pavle in Belgrade.
- Corpses of two newborn babies were found on Monday in a garbage dump in Mladenovac near Belgrade.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Only 30 percent of wheat area harvested in first week of July due to rains. Rains good for maize, sunflower, soybean, sugarbeet and other spring crops.
- Hail and draught badly damage Serbia's raspberry crop. Planned earnings of $50 million from raspberry exports will probably be halved.
- Around 3,500 invalids of the 1991-1995 wars on the territories of former Yugoslavia on the brink of subsistence. Lack of funds delays disablement pensions.
- Dispute between some 15 commercial banks and the National Bank of Yugoslavia over the central bank's decision to revoke their licenses due to insolvency still not resolved.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic reshuffled his government on Tuesday. New deputy prime ministers are Milutin Lalic and Jovan Mihailovic, Branko Perovic is foreign minister, Branislava Lijesevic culture minister and Branko Vujovic trade minister.

- The public prosecutor' office said in a release Tuesday no pressure had been put on the Ulcingj members of the Democratic Party of Socialists to vote for or against the holding of an extraordinary party congress.
- Pensions in Montenegro are overdue because the Yugoslav federation is late in paying its contribution. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
